lead: Movable things a household owns to keep people, property and the home safe: locks and padlocks, safes and key boxes, alarms and cameras, fire and leak detection, child-proofing and pest control, plus a locksport and lock-collecting department. Organised by the threat guarded against, then by what the object is; installed alarms, intercoms and window guards live in Home Fixtures.

depts.t: Locks, bolts, padlocks and deterrents that keep a door, window, gate or shed shut; a collectable or practice lock → Locksport & lock collecting; a box for valuables → Safes & key boxes.
depts.ax: Where is the protection fitted: built into the door, added onto a door or window, carried on a padlock, or placed around the property?

s.t: Lock bodies, cylinders and electronic locks built into a door, gate or cabinet, such as mortice locks, deadbolts and smart locks; a bolt or bar added on the surface → Add-on door, window & gate security.
s.ax: kinds by what is fitted: lock in the door edge, lock on the door face, bored-through lock, the loose cylinder, electronic locks, small cabinet locks

k.a: mortise lock · mortice deadlock · mortice sashlock · mortice latch
k.d: A lock case sunk into the door edge; a deadlock has a key-thrown bolt only, a sashlock adds a handle-worked latch, a latch has no bolt.

k.a: nightlatch · Yale lock · rim deadlock · rim sashlock
k.d: A surface-mounted lock on the inside face of a door, worked by a rim cylinder from outside and a knob or snib inside.

k.a: bore-through deadbolt · single-cylinder deadbolt · double-cylinder deadbolt
k.d: A North-American bolt lock fitted through a bored hole above the knob, thrown by key or thumb-turn, graded ANSI/BHMA 1–3.

k.a: entry knob · entry lever · handleset · door handle lockset
k.d: A knob or lever set with its own key cylinder fitted through the door, often paired with a deadbolt in a handleset.

k.a: multi-point door lock
k.d: Door lock that throws bolts or hooks into the frame at several points along the door edge.

k.a: euro cylinder · profile cylinder · rim cylinder · barrel · key cylinder
k.d: The key-operated barrel sold apart from the lock case; chosen by profile and by anti-snap, drill and bump rating.
see: restricted-key cylinders collected by lock pickers

k.a: connected lock · app lock · keyless smart deadbolt
k.d: An electromechanical door lock opened by phone, keypad, fingerprint or home-automation hub, as a retrofit module or a full replacement.

k.a: push-button lock · digital door lock · code lock · mechanical combination door lock
k.d: A door lock opened by a code on mechanical push buttons or an electronic keypad, with no app needed.

k.a: cam lock · drawer lock · locker lock · mailbox lock
k.d: A small keyed lock for a cupboard, drawer, locker or mailbox, turning a cam or small bolt.

s.t: Fittings screwed or clamped onto a door, window, gate or outbuilding as extra security, such as barrel bolts, door chains, window locks and shed bars; a lock built into the door → Door & cabinet locks.
s.ax: kinds by what they secure: a door, a patio door, a window, a gate or shutter, an outbuilding

k.a: sliding bolt · barrel bolt · tower bolt · flush bolt · rack bolt · pad bolt
k.d: A sliding bolt fixed to a door or gate to hold it shut, usually as secondary security behind the main lock.
see: the ironmongery bolt sold by the trade

k.a: door chain · security chain · swing-bar guard · door latch guard
k.d: A chain or hinged bar that lets a door open a few centimetres so a caller can be checked before it is released.

k.a: door jammer · portable door lock · travel door lock · door brace
k.d: A portable bar, floor brace or latch clip that holds an inward-opening door shut from inside without screws or drilling.

k.a: sliding door lock · French door bolt · patio bolt
k.d: An add-on lock or bolt for a sliding or French patio door, fitted to the frame or the meeting stiles.

k.a: sash lock · sash stop · casement lock · lockable window handle · window bolt
k.d: A keyed lock, stop or lockable handle fitted to a window sash or casement to stop it opening.

k.a: gate lock · bullet lock · garage door lock · shutter lock · long-throw lock
k.d: A lock made for a garden gate, up-and-over garage door or roller shutter, surface-mounted or set into the profile.

k.a: shed bar · garage door defender · ground anchor · padbar · wall anchor
k.d: Fixed steel bars, posts and anchors that secure shed, garage or outbuilding doors and anchor bikes or machinery.

s.t: Portable shackle locks and the hasps, chains and cables they close, such as the Master Lock No. 3 and ABUS Granit; a lock built into a door → Door & cabinet locks.
s.ax: kinds by what you buy: the padlock, its electronic version, the hasp it closes, the chain or cable it secures with

k.a: key padlock · combination padlock · shackle lock
k.d: A portable lock with a hinged or sliding shackle, secured by key or combination to a hasp, chain or cable.

k.a: smart padlock · Bluetooth padlock
k.d: A padlock opened by phone, NFC, fingerprint or a programmed electronic key instead of a metal key.

k.a: padlock hasp · hasp & staple
k.d: A hinged strap and fixed eye screwed to door and frame, through which a padlock is passed.

k.a: hardened chain · padlock chain
k.d: A hardened steel chain, usually sleeved, used with a padlock to secure gates, sheds, bikes or motorcycles.

k.a: security cable · coil lock
k.d: A flexible steel cable, often plastic-coated, with built-in or padlock closure for securing loose items.

s.t: Things that let you see a caller, strengthen glass, deter climbers or make stolen goods traceable, such as peephole viewers and window film; a camera that records → Cameras & recorders.
s.ax: kinds by how they deter: see the caller, strengthen the glass, stop climbing, make theft traceable

k.a: peephole · spyhole · door eye · digital door viewer
k.d: A lens or small camera fitted through a door so a caller can be seen from inside without opening it.
tt: Digital viewer with camera and screen
see: camera doorbell with a peephole form

k.a: safety film · anti-shatter film · glass protection film
k.d: A clear polyester film applied to glass to hold fragments together when the pane is struck or broken.

k.a: wall spike · fence spike · roller barrier · 忍び返し
k.d: Strips or rotating barriers fixed along a wall, fence or gate top to deter climbing; height limits and warning signs may apply locally.
tt: Plastic spike strip for fences and walls

k.a: forensic marking · UV marker · asset marking · SmartWater · SelectaDNA
k.d: A kit for marking valuables with a traceable code (forensic liquid, UV ink or etching) linked to an owner register such as Immobilise.
tt: Alarm or CCTV warning sign or sticker

depts.t: Lockable containers for valuables, papers, keys and post kept at home; the lock on a door → Locks & door security; a fire-fighting aid → Fire, gas & leak safety.
depts.ax: What is kept inside: valuables and papers, keys, or post and parcels?

s.t: Steel boxes for valuables, papers, cash or firearms, rated against theft or fire, such as wall safes, document chests and gun cabinets; a box for keys → Key boxes.
s.ax: kinds by the main threat they are built against: theft, fire, unauthorised access to firearms, discovery, loose cash

k.a: home safe · security safe · strongbox · 金庫
k.d: A steel strongbox with a certified burglary-resistant body and lock, kept at home to protect cash, jewellery and documents.
tt: UL RSC Level I to III

k.a: fireproof safe · fire chest · document box · fire file
k.d: A container rated to protect papers and media from fire for a stated time, from portable chests and bags to cabinets.

k.a: gun cabinet · firearms cabinet · rifle cabinet · pistol box · Waffenschrank
k.d: A lockable steel cabinet or safe made to store firearms and ammunition away from unauthorised hands.

k.a: hidden safe · book safe
k.d: A small safe built into an ordinary-looking object such as a book, can or wall outlet, hidden in plain sight.

k.a: petty cash box · money tin
k.d: A small portable lockable steel box with a coin tray for holding cash.

s.t: Small lockable holders for spare keys, outdoors or indoors, such as wall-mounted key safes and key cabinets; a box for post → Post & parcel boxes.

k.a: outdoor key box · key lock box · キーボックス
k.d: A small lockable box, usually wall-mounted outside, that holds a spare door key behind a code.

k.a: key box · key hook cabinet

see: outdoor box for one spare key

s.t: Boxes that receive letters or parcels and can be locked, such as wall letterboxes and drop-slot parcel boxes; a box for keys → Key boxes.

k.a: mailbox · post box
k.d: A box fixed to a wall, post or through a wall that receives letters and small post.

k.a: parcel drop box · package box · delivery box
k.d: A larger lockable box that lets couriers leave parcels securely when nobody is home.

depts.t: Devices that detect an intruder, record video or announce a caller; a professionally installed alarm → Home Fixtures; a smoke or gas alarm → Fire, gas & leak safety.
depts.ax: What does it do: sound an alarm on detection, record what happens, or announce a caller?

s.t: Self-fitted alarm kits, panels, detectors, sirens and personal alarms that sound when someone enters or attacks; a camera → Cameras & recorders.
s.ax: kinds from the whole system to its parts: kit, control panel, sensors, an outdoor approach alarm, a personal alarm

k.a: DIY alarm system · smart home alarm · self-install burglar alarm · hub-and-sensor alarm
k.d: Self-installed intruder alarm: a hub or base station with battery sensors, keypad and siren, controlled by app and monitored by the owner or a paid service.

k.a: alarm panel · alarm keypad
k.d: The unit that reads the sensors, tracks whether the alarm is set and sounds it, with the keypad or fob that sets and unsets it.

k.a: motion sensor · PIR detector · door and window contact · entry sensor · glass-break detector · shock sensor · stand-alone siren · panic button
k.d: A detector, siren or button that senses movement, opening, breaking glass or vibration and sounds locally or signals an alarm hub.

k.a: driveway sensor · approach alarm
k.d: A sensor and receiver that sound a chime when a vehicle or person approaches along a drive or path.

k.a: personal safety alarm · rape alarm · keyring alarm · panic alarm
k.d: A hand-held or keyring device that emits a very loud siren, sometimes with a strobe, to shock an attacker and attract attention.

s.t: Cameras that record or stream video of the home and the recorders that store it, such as indoor Wi-Fi cameras, floodlight cameras and wired recorder systems; a doorbell with a camera → Doorbells.

k.a: home security camera · IP camera · Wi-Fi camera · indoor cam · outdoor cam · dummy camera · fake security camera
k.d: A standalone network camera, indoor or outdoor, that records or streams video of the home to an app or local storage.

k.a: floodlight cam · spotlight camera · security light camera
k.d: A security camera combined with a motion-activated LED floodlight, wired or battery, for driveways and yards.

k.a: NVR kit · DVR kit · CCTV system · PoE camera system · camera system kit · network video recorder
k.d: A recorder (NVR or DVR) sold with several wired cameras as one system, storing video locally on a hard drive.

s.t: Buttons and sounders that announce a caller, with or without a camera; a camera that only watches → Cameras & recorders.

k.a: smart doorbell · doorbell camera · peephole camera
k.d: An internet-connected doorbell with a camera, microphone and motion sensor that shows, records and lets you talk to callers from a phone.
see: fixed intercom at the gate or door

k.a: door chime · wireless doorbell · bell push
k.d: A push button with a sounder that announces a caller, without a camera; wired to a transformer or a radio-linked wireless kit.

depts.t: Detectors and fire-fighting aids for the home: smoke, heat, carbon monoxide, gas and water alarms, extinguishers, blankets and escape ladders; an intruder alarm → Alarms, cameras & doorbells.
depts.ax: Does it warn that a hazard is present, or help to put out a fire and escape from it?

k.a: regulatory sign

depts.t: Traps, baits, sprays, repellents and screens that kill or keep out household rodents, birds and insects; a spray for protecting garden plants → Feeds, sprays & plant protection.
depts.ax: What is the pest: a rodent, bird or other animal, or an insect?

s.t: Traps, baits, repellers and deterrents for mice, rats, birds and other animals around the home; a product for insects → Insects.
s.ax: kinds by method: kill with a trap, catch alive, poison, scare off

k.a: mouse trap · rat trap · snap trap · glue board · electronic rat trap
k.d: A trap that kills a mouse or rat by spring, sticky board or electric shock.

k.a: humane trap · cage trap · live trap
k.d: A wire cage trap that catches a rodent or small animal alive for release.

k.a: rat poison · mouse bait · bait box · tamper-resistant bait station · bait station key
k.d: Poison bait for mice and rats, and the lockable box that holds it so only the pest can reach it.

k.a: ultrasonic pest repeller · rodent repellent · moth repellent · mothballs · cedar block
k.d: A device or substance set around the home to drive rodents, insects or moths away without trapping or killing them.

k.a: bird spikes · pigeon spikes · bird netting · bird gel · bird scarer · decoy owl
k.d: Netting, spikes, coils, gel dishes or decoys fitted on ledges, roofs and gardens to stop birds landing or nesting.

s.t: Sprays, baits, traps, vaporisers and screens for flies, wasps, mosquitoes, ants, cockroaches and moths; a product for rodents or birds → Rodents, birds & animals.
s.ax: kinds by method: spray or bait to kill, trap, swat, repel from the air, screen out

k.a: bug spray · fly spray · insect killer · bug bomb
k.d: A ready-to-use chemical that kills insects on contact or by residue, sold as spray, foam, dust or room fogger.

k.a: ant bait · cockroach bait · bait station · gel bait
k.d: A poisoned food in gel, paste, granule or station form that ants, cockroaches or similar carry back to the nest.

k.a: wasp trap · fruit fly trap · moth trap · fly paper · glue trap
k.d: A sticky, baited, pheromone or light trap that lures and holds flying or crawling insects.

k.a: fly swat · bug zapper · electric fly swatter · insect killer lamp
k.d: A hand paddle, electrified racket or UV-lamp grid that kills flies and other insects by swatting or electrocution.

k.a: plug-in mosquito killer · mosquito repellent device · mosquito coil · vaporiser refill
k.d: A plug-in, battery or burning device that releases insecticide into room or patio air to kill or repel mosquitoes.

k.a: bed net · fly screen · magnetic door screen · window mesh
k.d: A hanging net or loose-fitting mesh that keeps insects off a sleeper or out of a window or door opening.

ax: What is the object protecting against: a person getting in, theft of valuables, fire or leaks, a child being hurt, or pests?
key: 1. Is it a lock or tool kept or used as a hobby: a collectable or antique lock, a practice lock or a pick set? → Locksport & lock collecting
2. Does it keep a door, window, gate or shed shut, show who is at the door or deter a climber? → Locks & door security
3. Is it a locked box for valuables, papers, keys, post or parcels? → Safes & key boxes
4. Does it detect an intruder, record video or announce a caller? → Alarms, cameras & doorbells
5. Does it warn of, or fight, fire, carbon monoxide, gas or a leak? → Fire, gas & leak safety
6. Is it for keeping a child from a hazard or listening to a baby? → Child & home safety
7. Does it trap, bait, repel or screen out rodents, birds or insects? → Pest & insect control

Precedence: a lock you fit to your own door is a door lock (step 2) even when a collector prizes the make; a smart lock is a lock (step 2) before an alarm (step 4); a video doorbell is a doorbell (step 4); a fire-resistant safe is a safe (step 3); a mosquito net is pest control (step 7); a baby monitor is child safety (step 6).
